sections.title: konyha means more than just "kitchen"
sections.content: You already know *konyha* as "kitchen", but Hungarian also uses it the way English uses "cuisine" — *a magyar konyha* is "Hungarian food" as a whole tradition, not just a room. *fűszer* ("spice") and *paprika* (Hungary's most famous one) are what let you talk about what makes it distinctive (*fűszer* is the new word; you know *paprika* from the A1 market) — and both pair naturally with the definite forms from the screen before.

items.spanish: Károly nagyon szereti a magyar konyhát.
A magyar ételekben sok fűszer van, leginkább paprika.
items.english: There's a lot of spice in Hungarian food, mostly paprika.

items.spanish: Eszi a levest, mert sok jó fűszer van a levesben.
items.english: He's eating the soup, because there's a lot of good spice in the soup.

sections.content: *szereti a magyar konyhát* is definite — *a magyar konyhát* names one specific, known thing (Hungarian cuisine as a whole concept), the same logic as *eszi a levest* from the screen before, just with *szeret* instead of *eszik*.
